To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the competition climate is perceived as positive by 50% of the participants, as negative by 25% and as null by the remaining 25%, (2) there is no difference in the performance of the participants in terms of time, distance and number of laps, and (3) there is a significant positive effect of a positive competition climate on the performance of the children.

The results showed a significant difference between the performance of students who felt a positive sense of competition and the performance of those who felt a neutral or negative sense of competition.

1) the students' perception of the competition influenced their running time; 2) students who perceived the competition in a positive way ran faster than those who perceived the competition as neutral or negative; and 3) students who perceived competition negatively ran slower than students who perceived the situation in a positive way or in a neutral way.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the question of whether competition is beneficial for performance in a sport setting.
the question of how the perception of competition influences the performance of 6-year-old students in the context of a running race.
the influence that competition may have on performance in elementary school children.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the competition can influence performance in children but the influence is not the same for all children.
the competition is an effective tool to enhance the performance of children in a running task.
competition is a double-edged sword.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the competition is a powerful tool to increase the motivation of students to improve their performance.
we found a significant positive relationship between the feeling of competition and performance.
the positive feelings about competition are related to the increase in the children's performance.

the competition is a tool that can be used in the classroom.
